key_terms.meaning: A rule ⟨u, v⟩ giving a real (or complex) number for each pair of vectors, with ⟨v, v⟩ ≥ 0 and ⟨v, v⟩ = 0 only for v = 0, plus symmetry and linearity in each slot.
The length of a vector, ‖v‖ = √⟨v, v⟩; always ≥ 0, and ‖cv‖ = |c| ‖v‖.
On Rⁿ, ⟨u, v⟩ = u₁v₁ + u₂v₂ + … + uₙvₙ, written u · v.
d(u, v) = ‖u − v‖, the length of the difference vector.
cos θ = ⟨u, v⟩ / (‖u‖ ‖v‖) for nonzero u and v; θ is measured in radians.
|⟨u, v⟩| ≤ ‖u‖ ‖v‖, with equality exactly when one vector is a scalar multiple of the other.
‖u + v‖ ≤ ‖u‖ + ‖v‖; the direct route is never longer than the detour.
Vectors u and v with ⟨u, v⟩ = 0; perpendicular in the geometric sense.
A set where every vector has norm 1 and every pair is orthogonal: ⟨uᵢ, uⱼ⟩ = 1 if i = j, 0 otherwise.
For a subspace W of V, W⊥ = {v in V : ⟨v, w⟩ = 0 for every w in W}; itself a subspace.
A step-by-step recipe that replaces a basis v₁, …, vₙ by an orthonormal basis u₁, …, uₙ spanning the same spaces.

key_terms.term: Orthogonal projection of b onto W
key_terms.meaning: The unique vector proj_W b in W with b − proj_W b in W⊥; when u₁, …, uₖ is an orthonormal basis of W, proj_W b = Σᵢ ⟨b, uᵢ⟩ uᵢ.
The system AᵀA x = Aᵀb, whose solutions are exactly the least squares solutions of Ax = b.
A vector x̂ that minimises ‖b − Ax‖; used when Ax = b has no exact solution.
A = QR, where A is m × n with independent columns, Q is m × n with orthonormal columns, and R is n × n upper triangular with positive diagonal.
The numbers σ₁ ≥ σ₂ ≥ … ≥ σᵣ > 0 equal to the square roots of the nonzero eigenvalues of AᵀA.
A = UΣVᵀ, with U and V orthogonal and Σ diagonal holding the singular values in decreasing order.
The number of nonzero singular values of A; also the number of nonzero pivots in row echelon form.
For an invertible matrix, κ(A) = σ_max / σ_min; a large value means small input errors can cause large output errors.
Cutting the SVD after k terms gives Aₖ = Σᵢ₌₁ᵏ σᵢ uᵢ vᵢᵀ, the best rank-k approximation of A in the Frobenius norm.

takeaways: An inner product is the single extra rule that gives a vector space the ideas of length, distance and angle.
Cauchy–Schwarz is the engine behind the triangle inequality, the angle formula and every bound on projection error.
Orthonormal vectors behave like a clean coordinate system: coefficients are found by dot products, with no equations to solve.
Gram–Schmidt is bookkeeping, not magic: each new vector loses its parts along the directions already fixed.
The closest point of a subspace to b is the orthogonal projection of b, and its error vector is perpendicular to the subspace.
Least squares replaces the unsolvable Ax = b by the always-solvable normal equations AᵀAx = Aᵀb.
QR decomposition is Gram–Schmidt written in matrix form, and it is the numerically safe way to solve least squares.
SVD works for every matrix, square or rectangular, and orders the directions by how much the matrix stretches them.
The ratio σ_max / σ_min, the condition number, tells you how much a linear system can magnify round-off error.
bank_note: Long answers here are usually proof-plus-computation: state the definition or theorem, prove it in general, then carry the same idea through a small R² or R³ example with numbers shown at every step.

bank.q: Define an inner product on a real vector space by listing its axioms. Show that ⟨u, v⟩ = 2u₁v₁ + 3u₂v₂ is an inner product on R², and compute the norm of (1, 1) and the angle between (1, 0) and (0, 1) under this inner product.
outline: Four axioms: symmetry, additivity, scalar pull-out, positive definiteness
Check each axiom for the weighted formula
cos θ = 0, so θ = π/2

bank.q: State and prove the Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for a real inner product space, and use it to derive the triangle inequality for the norm.
outline: Statement |⟨u, v⟩| ≤ ‖u‖‖v‖
Proof by considering ‖u − t v‖² ≥ 0 as a quadratic in t, or the projection argument
Equality case
Triangle inequality from ‖u + v‖² = ‖u‖² + 2⟨u, v⟩ + ‖v‖²

bank.q: Define an orthogonal set and an orthonormal set. Prove that a nonzero orthogonal set is linearly independent, and hence that an orthonormal set is a basis for the space it spans.
outline: Definitions with ⟨uᵢ, uⱼ⟩ = 0 and ‖uᵢ‖ = 1
Take Σ cᵢuᵢ = 0 and dot with uⱼ
Get cⱼ‖uⱼ‖² = 0, so cⱼ = 0
Conclusion: independence; span gives a basis

bank.q: For a subspace W of Rⁿ, define W⊥. Prove that W⊥ is a subspace of Rⁿ, that W ∩ W⊥ = {0}, and state the relation dim W + dim W⊥ = n.
outline: Definition of W⊥
Closure under addition and scalar multiplication
Intersection argument using ⟨v, v⟩ = 0
Dimension statement and why it holds

bank.q: Apply the Gram–Schmidt process to v₁ = (1, 1, 0), v₂ = (1, 0, 1), v₃ = (0, 1, 1) in R³ with the dot product, and obtain an orthonormal basis. Show every intermediate vector.
outline: u₁ = v₁, normalise
u₂ = v₂ − ⟨v₂, e₁⟩e₁
u₃ = v₃ − ⟨v₃, e₁⟩e₁ − ⟨v₃, e₂⟩e₂
Normalise and verify pairwise orthogonality

bank.q: Find the orthogonal projection of b = (1, 2, 3) onto the plane W: x + y + z = 0 in R³, the closest point of W to b, and the distance from b to W.
outline: Orthonormal basis of W or use the normal vector n = (1,1,1)
b − proj_W b = (⟨b, n⟩/‖n‖²) n = 2n, so proj = b − 2n
Distance = ‖2n‖ = 2√3

bank.q: Fit a straight line y = a + bx by least squares to the points (0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 5). Set up the matrix form Ax = b, derive the normal equations, and find a and b.
outline: A with columns of ones and x-values; b as data vector
AᵀA and Aᵀb computed explicitly
Solve the 2 × 2 system
State the fitted line and check residuals

bank.q: Find the QR decomposition of A = [[1, 1], [1, 0], [0, 1]] using Gram–Schmidt on the columns, and verify that A = QR with Q having orthonormal columns and R upper triangular.
outline: q₁ = a₁/‖a₁‖
r₁₂ = ⟨a₂, q₁⟩, q₂ from the residual, r₂₂ = residual norm
Assemble R = [[r₁₁, r₁₂], [0, r₂₂]] and multiply back

bank.q: Compute the SVD of A = [[1, 2], [2, 4]]. Find AᵀA, its eigenvalues and unit eigenvectors, the singular values, the matrices U, Σ, V, and write the best rank-1 approximation of A.
outline: AᵀA = [[5, 10], [10, 20]], eigenvalues 25 and 0
u₁ = Av₁/σ₁
Rank-1 term σ₁u₁v₁ᵀ equals A itself here, since rank A = 1

bank.q: A 2 × 2 matrix A has singular values σ₁ = 100 and σ₂ = 0.5. Compute the condition number, and explain what it means when Ax = b is solved on a computer with numbers rounded to 7 digits.
outline: κ = σ_max/σ_min = 200
Large κ means relative error in b can be amplified by up to about κ
Relative error estimate ≈ κ × machine precision
Practical remark: check residuals, or use QR/SVD instead of forming AᵀA

bank.q: Let u₁, …, uₖ be an orthonormal basis of a subspace W of Rⁿ. Prove that proj_W b = Σ ⟨b, uᵢ⟩ uᵢ, that b − proj_W b lies in W⊥, and that this vector is the unique closest point of W to b.
outline: Write the candidate p = Σ ⟨b, uᵢ⟩uᵢ and show p ∈ W
Show ⟨b − p, uⱼ⟩ = 0 for every j, hence b − p ∈ W⊥
For any w in W, ‖b − w‖² = ‖b − p‖² + ‖p − w‖² by Pythagoras
Minimum exactly at w = p, and p is unique

bank.q: Prove that the normal equations AᵀAx = Aᵀb are always consistent for any real m × n matrix A and any b in Rᵐ, and describe the set of all least squares solutions in terms of the null space of AᵀA.
outline: Aᵀb lies in the column space of Aᵀ
col(Aᵀ) = col(AᵀA), so consistency follows
Least squares solutions form x̂ + null(AᵀA)
null(AᵀA) = null(A), so uniqueness iff columns of A are independent
Reasoning via orthogonality of the residual to col(A)

bank.q: Show how the Gram–Schmidt process on the columns of an m × n matrix A with independent columns produces A = QR, explain why R is upper triangular with positive diagonal, and argue why this is numerically safer than solving the normal equations.
outline: Column-by-column construction, coefficients collected as rᵢⱼ
Triangular shape because aⱼ depends only on q₁, …, qⱼ
Positive diagonal from the normalisation step
Uniqueness when A has full column rank
Forming AᵀA squares the condition number; QR does not

bank.q: State the SVD theorem for an m × n matrix. Using A = UΣVᵀ, prove that the columns of U are an orthonormal basis of col(A), the columns of V corresponding to zero singular values span null(A), and rank(A) equals the number of nonzero singular values.
outline: Statement with sizes of U, Σ, V
A vᵢ = σᵢuᵢ, Aᵀuᵢ = σᵢvᵢ
Nonzero σ give a basis of col(A); zero σ directions give null(A)
Rank = count of nonzero σ
Optional: mention rank + nullity = n

glossary.def: A symmetric, additive, positively definite pairing ⟨u, v⟩ that produces a scalar from two vectors.
The standard inner product on Rⁿ, u · v = u₁v₁ + … + uₙvₙ.
The non-negative number ‖v‖ = √⟨v, v⟩ giving the length of v.
A vector whose norm is 1; any nonzero v gives the unit vector v / ‖v‖.
d(u, v) = ‖u − v‖, the length of the straight segment between the two vectors.
|⟨u, v⟩| ≤ ‖u‖‖v‖ for all vectors u and v.
‖u + v‖ ≤ ‖u‖ + ‖v‖, the norm version of 'a straight line is shortest'.
If ⟨u, v⟩ = 0 then ‖u + v‖² = ‖u‖² + ‖v‖².
‖u + v‖² + ‖u − v‖² = 2‖u‖² + 2‖v‖², true in every inner product space.
Having inner product zero; written u ⊥ v.
Both orthogonal to each other and of unit length.
A basis whose vectors are orthonormal, so coordinates are found by inner products alone.
W⊥, the set of all vectors orthogonal to every vector of the subspace W.
For an orthonormal set u₁, …, uₖ, Σ ⟨v, uᵢ⟩² ≤ ‖v‖², with equality for a basis.
For an orthonormal basis, ‖v‖² = Σ ⟨v, uᵢ⟩²; energy is preserved by the coordinates.
An algorithm converting a basis into an orthonormal basis by subtracting projections step by step.
The shadow proj_W b of b on W, the unique vector of W whose difference with b is in W⊥.
AᵀA x = Aᵀb, the square system solved to get least squares fits.
Any x̂ minimising the residual length ‖b − A x̂‖.
A factorisation A = QR with Q having orthonormal columns and R upper triangular.
A non-negative number σᵢ = √λᵢ, where λᵢ is an eigenvalue of AᵀA.
The factorisation A = UΣVᵀ valid for every real matrix.
The dimension of the column space; the number of nonzero singular values or nonzero pivots.
κ(A) = σ_max / σ_min for an invertible matrix, measuring sensitivity to small changes in data.
A truncated SVD sum Aₖ = Σᵢ₌₁ᵏ σᵢ uᵢ vᵢᵀ, optimal among matrices of rank k.
